central_question: Internal: why do people naturally do this? Crossover: what human tendency is being activated, and how was the system designed around it?
audience: 18-44. Psychology and science viewers, business and design viewers, productivity audiences, technology users, explainer and curiosity channel viewers. High international potential.

format.tone: Calm, mechanical, curious, dry, non-moralising. No outrage narrator. No 'companies are evil' simplification. No fake certainty about contested psychology. The narrator sounds like a person with a marker explaining a machine.

episode_structure.purpose: What people normally assume, dismissed quickly.
What is actually happening in attention, memory, social processing or perception.
What the mechanism helped people do.
Crossover episodes only: how an app, shop, interface or institution uses that tendency.
The exact point where natural behaviour becomes directed behaviour.
How to notice it next time.
Locked closing line, variant by family.

sign_off: Crossover: 'Your reaction was human. The setup was by design.' Pure psychology: 'You are not malfunctioning. You are behaving by design.'
editorial_split: Family A 'Built into you' (psychology, evolution, attention, memory, social behaviour, perception) and Family B 'Built around you' (retail design, pricing, software, interfaces, offices, airports, subscriptions, institutions). Long-term balance 50/50 — this split is also a revenue decision.

visual_style.style_string: Diagram-first sketch animation on faint graph paper: a light grid ground, always visible, never dominant. Monochrome hand-drawn linework with hand-drawn boxes and arrows. Simplified stick figures: large circular head, dot eyes, thick brow lines, minimal bodies. Chunky flat single-colour objects. Interface mock-ups, isometric physical spaces, flowcharts and behaviour loops drawn as tidy marker diagrams. Exactly one controlled red (#D62828) highlight per frame marking only the behavioural trigger, design choice, moment of manipulation, hidden incentive, or mechanism — never decorative. No shading, no gradients, no photorealism, no cartoon exaggeration.
visual_style.ground: Faint graph paper grid, always visible, never dominant
visual_style.accent: Red, one controlled highlight per frame
visual_style.accent_rule: Red marks only the behavioural trigger, the design choice, the moment of manipulation, the hidden incentive, or the mechanism itself. Never decorative. This single rule is the channel's whole visual identity.
frame_vocabulary: stick figures (large circular head, dot eyes, thick brows)
visual_style.motion: Progressive drawing. Elements appear in sequence as the narrator reaches them, then the red mark lands — that beat is the payoff of every segment. Only a handful of genuinely moving sequences per episode.

thumbnails.formula: One object or figure, one red mark, one short phrase, large negative space. No collages, no exaggerated faces.

disclaimer_block: This video is educational. It describes research on human behaviour and how products and environments are designed around it. Findings noted as contested are contested. Nothing here is medical or psychological advice.

shorts.source_beat: The recognition beat and the red-mark beat — where this format's viral potential lives

cadence.long_form_per_week: 3 (4 only if quality holds after day 46)

rpm_estimate_usd: RPM $5-13, CPM $10-26. Higher on the Built Around You half (money, software, business, consumer decisions); lower on broad psychology.
